summary: @servicetitan/responsive preinstall drops Bun runtime to execute an undeclared obfuscated 720KB payload
details: The package declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`, which runs automatically on `npm install`. setup.mjs is itself obfuscated (hex-named identifiers `_0x488df8`, per-function string-key indirection dictionaries wrapping literals and calls). It downloads the Bun runtime from `github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases`, extracts it to a temporary directory, marks it executable, and invokes it against `math_init.js` at the tarball root via `execFileSync(bun, [path.join(D,'math_init.js')], {cwd:D})`. `math_init.js` is a 727,680-byte heavily obfuscated file (string-array rotation function, large numeric/char table, machine-generated identifiers) that is NOT declared in `package.json.files` (which lists only `dist` and `src`), so it is smuggled outside the manifest surface. The advertised purpose is a React responsive-components library, which has no legitimate need for a second language runtime at install time or for executing a large obfuscated sibling script. Fetching an alternate runtime specifically to execute a package-local obfuscated payload is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern — it hides execution from Node-based install-time scanners.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
